---
title: "Build and publish documentation"
---

Edit QMD pages and Python docstrings, then push to `main`. After the one-time
Pages setup, GitHub Actions builds and publishes the site automatically.
Pull requests build the same site for validation without deploying it.

## 1. Enable GitHub Pages once

In `ysBach/ndfiltrs`, open **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment** and
select **GitHub Actions** as the source. The `github-pages` environment must
allow deployments from `main`; add reviewers only if you want manual approval
on each deployment.

The published URL is <https://ysbach.github.io/ndfiltrs/>. Pushes to `main`
and manual runs from `main` deploy only in the canonical repository. Forks
and pull requests build without publishing.

## 2. Install the documentation tools

Install [Quarto 1.9.37](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) and `uv`, then run
from the repository root:

```bash
uv venv .venv-docs --python 3.13
uv pip install --python .venv-docs/bin/python -r docs/requirements-quarto.txt
```

This dedicated environment contains only the static documentation tools.
These commands do not synchronize or modify the shared scientific environment.

## 3. Edit the maintained sources

Edit the source Markdown guides and Python docstrings. The build adds short
introductions to generated website copies without modifying the source guides.

| Content | Edit |
| --- | --- |
| Landing page, quickstart, or this guide | `docs/quarto/*.qmd` |
| Filtering, convolution, repair, or benchmark guide | Existing `docs/*.md` |
| Function signature or reference details | Python source in `python/ndfiltrs/` |
| Navigation and API groups | `docs/quarto/_quarto.yml` |

The build stages the existing Markdown guides into QMD and rewrites their
relative links. The maintained `docs/quarto/guides/index.qmd` is committed;
the other guide QMD files and `docs/quarto/api/` pages are generated and
ignored by Git. Edit the canonical Markdown to change a generated guide.

## 4. Build or preview locally

```bash
make docs-build
make docs-preview
```

`docs-build` regenerates the guides and API before rendering the whole site
to `docs/quarto/_site/`. `docs-preview` also regenerates those pages before
starting Quarto preview. If you change a source docstring or a canonical
`docs/*.md` guide while preview is open, run `make docs-api` in another terminal.
Use `DOCS_PYTHON=/absolute/path/to/python` to select an existing documentation
environment explicitly.

Static API generation reads source signatures and docstrings without importing
`ndfiltrs`, so the documentation build does not need a compiled native extension.

Plain Python snippets are not executed by Quarto. When editing an example,
run it locally against the matching built extension, including its assertions.
Native package behavior remains covered by the package test workflow.

## 5. Publish and inspect the result

Commit the maintained sources, push to `main`, and inspect the **Docs**
workflow. Its build artifact is the rendered site; a successful deployment
updates the Pages URL. No registry release or PyPI upload is required.

The site describes `main`, not necessarily the latest published version.
The workflow deploys only after the documentation build succeeds. An earlier
site remains online if a later build fails.
